"Observing Chóngwēi's demeanor and actions,
he surely has treacherous intentions.
Everyone on the road says Guō Wēi has already become emperor,
yet Your Majesty continues to advance deep into enemy territory.
Disaster is imminent!
I urgently request to summon Zhāng Lìngchāo,
explain the situation of fortune and disaster to him,
and have him use his troops tonight to ambush Chóngwēi,
and seize his soldiers.
Tomorrow,
plunder the gold and silk of Suīyáng,
recruit soldiers,
and flee north to Jìnyáng.
Sòngzhōu
is Suīyáng Commandery.
Liú Yǔn's father, Liú Chóng, was stationed at Jìnyáng.
Suī,
yīn suī.
Zǒu,
yīn zòu.
Before they have time to pursue us,
this is the best strategy!"
Liú Yǔn hesitated and could not decide.
That night,
Guō Chóngwēi secretly persuaded Zhāng Lìngchāo,
and Lìngchāo led his troops to join him.
Liú Yǔn was greatly frightened.
Guō Wēi sent a letter to Liú Yǔn,
saying he was forced by the various armies;
he summoned Féng Dào to return first,
leaving Zhào Shàngjiāo and Wáng Dù to attend upon him.
When Dào took his leave,
Liú Yǔn said:
"The reason I came here relying on you
is because you have been chancellor for thirty years,
so I had no doubts.
Féng Dào
became chancellor in the second year of Tiānchéng of Táng Míngzōng,
until now twenty-four years.
Saying thirty years
is a rounded number.
Yí,
Yú Jì fān.
The situation is perilous.
What plan do you have?"
Dào remained silent.
Having no answer for Liú Yǔn,
he remained silent.
Féng Dào called himself a foolish and stubborn old man;
indeed, he was not wrong.
They wanted to kill him.
Liú Yǔn said:
"Do not act rashly.
This has nothing to do with Lord Féng."
When the Khitan ruler entered Biàn,
he reprimanded Liú Jìxūn,
and Jìxūn blamed Dào,
and Dào nearly died.
In the affair at Sòngzhōu,
had Liú Yǔn followed Jiǎ Zhēn's suggestion,
Dào would also certainly have died.
Yet the Khitan ruler said Dào was not a troublemaker,
and Liú Yǔn said it had nothing to do with Lord Féng.
Was this not because during his tenure he always maintained a humble and indifferent demeanor,
and did not compete with others,
so people all respected his reputation and virtue, and thus acted this way!
That Dào preserved his life
was indeed fortunate for him,
but how could a ruler employ such a chancellor!
However, since the Tóngguāng period of the Later Táng,
the Privy Councilors handled affairs,
and the Chancellors merely filled their positions.
Blaming others is not difficult;
it is only accepting blame that flows like water.
In this regard,
Dào was unwilling to accept blame.
They killed several of his close associates, including Dǒng Yì and Jiǎ Zhēn.
On the Jǐwèi day,
the Empress Dowager issued an edict,
demoting Liú Yǔn to Duke of Xiāngyīn.
Mǎ Duó led troops into Xǔzhōu,
and Liú Xìn, terrified and confused, committed suicide.
On the Gēngshēn day,
the Empress Dowager issued an edict,
appointing the Palace Attendant to oversee state affairs.
Both edicts issued by the Empress Dowager
were in accordance with Guō Wēi’s intentions.
The Palace Attendant
referred to Guō Wēi’s official title.
On the Rénxū night,
a drunken infantry commander in the camp of the overseer of state affairs
boasted that the cavalry in Chánzhōu had previously supported the enthronement,
and now the infantry also wished to do the same.
The overseer of state affairs executed him.
The ruler of Southern Hàn appointed palace attendants Lú Qióngxiān and Huáng Qióngzhī as female Palace Attendants,
dressed in court attire and official regalia,
to participate in decision-making on state affairs.
The imperial clan and veteran meritorious officials
were almost entirely executed,
leaving only eunuchs such as Lín Yányù and others in power.
History records that Southern Hàn ultimately perished due to eunuchs and female favorites,
and the reason the ruler of Southern Hàn was able to maintain his reign until the end
was because he was situated in a remote coastal region,
while the Central Plains lacked a true sovereign.
Punctuated by Róng Zhàozǔ, proofread by Niè Chóngqí.
